newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke - mark's slide vs dlr must slow.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke - mark's slide vs dlr must slow.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said that he saw no danger that inflation would be imported into Germany due to the dollar's recent strong appreciation against the mark.
Speaking to journalists after a news conference, Welteke also said that the mark could not continue to depreciate against the dollar at the pace seen over the last few days.
But he added that the mark's depreciation against the dollar had helped to boost German exports.
Buba's Welteke-mark's slide vs dollar must slow =2
"The D-mark depreciation cannot continue at the pace at which at his been going," Welteke said, admitting however that a slight further depreciation would be possible.
He said that the appreciation of the dollar was currently helping the German economy, providing the "only ray of light" for German economic growth.
But he added that economic growth of two to 2.5 percent for 1997 was realistic. Yet even this would not be sufficient to significantly improve the situation on Germany's labour market, he said.
German joblessness is currently running at a record level of more than four million.
